claim: The pre-registered S6 measurement-validity item failed in both policies (27,376/293,614 and 26,891/286,925 pair-rows differ by more than 1 mm); the failure stands.
condition_or_limit: Exploratory item of the C1 spec; not a primary hypothesis

claim: Most S6 disagreements involve listed proximity pairs, not contacts: 99% of compared rows have zero impulse and 83% of the over-tolerance rows are pairs 10-40 mm apart; near contact (PhysX separation <= 1 mm) 1.3% of rows exceed 1 mm.
condition_or_limit: Descriptive over dependent rows; scene-bootstrap intervals given

claim: For most pair kinds the PhysX separations agree better with poses about one physics sub-step before the logged pose (median residual of over-tolerance rows from ~5 mm to <0.2 mm in 6 of 9 kinds), consistent with a time offset between the contact list and the logged pose.
condition_or_limit: EXPLANATORY_ONLY; constant-velocity interpolation is an assumption; PhysX internal order not observed

claim: The time offset is not the only cause: static pairs (relative speed < 1 mm/s) still exceed 1 mm in 4,201 rows, slow finger-cube rows keep a ~1.8 mm residual, and camera-cube rows are unexplained.
A PhysX point separation is a per-manifold-point quantity and is not in general the minimum shape distance S6 compared it with.
condition_or_limit: Shown for slow finger rows only partly (ray matches for 56% of points); not resolved for every point

claim: The reconstruction geometry is correct for boxes: 19 closed-form cases and transform tests pass to 1e-9 m for the existing and an independent path, and the two paths agree to 3e-13 mm on every box pair kind of 8,394 real rows.
condition_or_limit: Box shapes only; no closed form for meshes

claim: The logged PhysX convex meshes are not triangulated as convex hulls; the existing calculator's distances for the hand therefore differ by up to 0.24 mm from the convex hull of the same vertices.
condition_or_limit: A small reconstruction error; affects hand pairs (and arm-link audits not re-analysed)

claim: All Check 4 failures (V2 9/41 and 5/39; 110 of 715 moves over all arms) occur only at the first control step and only on the direction condition; from the second step on no move fails (POST_HOC_STEP2PLUS 0/715).

Check 4 failures did not coincide with harm in C1: 0 of 14 V2 failures (0 of 110 overall) are harm; every harm move (51157 seed 1, 51253 seed 2) passed Check 4.
